description: Check the page border, soft shadow and tinted glow in native Appearance settings.
preconditions: Build and package the exact candidate as an isolated Dev app with the mock Keychain.
Use a plain light page and a plain dark page to distinguish the page edge from its effect.
steps: Open Appearance and find Page edge. Verify the default has Border 0, a black shadow, 25% opacity, Blur 8, Vertical offset 2, Horizontal offset 0 and Spread 0.
Change Border between 0 and 6. Inspect every corner and verify the ordinary page does not reflow.
Select Soft shadow, Glow and None. Change opacity, blur, color, each offset and spread; verify live changes. Confirm the presets preserve the chosen border.
Open Shadow details and check negative offsets and spread. Set Blur 0 and positive spread; verify no opaque black source shape appears behind the effect.
Create a side-by-side split and switch the focused pane. Inspect both pages and the divider for selection outlines and unwanted shadow over the pages. Repeat with a stacked split when available.
Collapse the sidebar, hide the top bar, resize the window and enter and exit fullscreen. Check that the shadow follows the page corners and remains outside the page.
Choose Use Arc style and confirm Border 0 and the default subtle black shadow return together.
Set a custom border and tinted glow. Quit normally and relaunch the same profile, then reopen Settings and verify the saved controls and visible effect.
Stop the isolated app normally and inspect for a new matching crash report.
observables: The default page has rounded corners and a soft shadow, with no decorative hairline.
Border is independently adjustable from 0 to 6 logical pixels. Page margin retains the previous frame-inset behavior.
The effect is behind all pages and never washes over page content, including transparent content. Split focus and capture outlines remain meaningful.
Managed and unavailable preferences reject edits without changing saved values.
The custom border and all shadow values survive normal relaunch; teardown produces no new matching crash.
